description: Eurorack power inlet
notes: 16-PIN A-100 BUS HEADER, AND ITS +5V IS NOT USED (owner, 2026-09-30: 'We keep the standard header, we just don't use the 5 volt. This keeps commonality of all the Eurorack cable connectors.'; ADR 0023 point 3). Pins 11-12 (+5V) and 13-16 (CV, Gate) have pads and no net: no-connects on the sheet. The module's 5V is U-REG-LOGIC. XFCN BH254V-16P, LCSC C492443 [ds XFCN-BH254V-16P-2x8-BOX-HEADER.pdf]. -12V IS THE RED STRIPE and pin 1: mark it on the silkscreen. A KEYED SHROUD DOES NOT MAKE A REVERSED RIBBON IMPOSSIBLE - Doepfer's own bus boards are unkeyed, 'red strip down' [ds DOEPFER-A100-TECHNICAL-DETAILS-a100t_e.html]. description: 8-conductor ruggedised connector, the module panel's end of the umbilical
package: THROUGH-HOLE, vertical PCB, rear panel mount (woody:Neutrik_NE8FAV_etherCON_Vertical)
notes: THE MODULE END (ADR 0023): the same part as the instrument's J-UMBILICAL-INST (ADR 0021), soldered straight into the module's main board - no adapter, no patch lead. LCSC C368526 [web 2026-09-29]. Its flange face sets the main board's depth behind the panel (config/body.yaml ethercon.pcb_setback), which is why the module is two boards (PCB-MODULE, PCB-MODULE-JACK). PANEL: the 22 mm bore, the two screws and a slot for the PUSH tab, which stands in front of the flange above the bore (config/body.yaml ethercon.tab_*) - from the NE8FAV drawing and STEP, test-fitted on the first panel. description: Schottky reverse polarity protection
notes: ~0.3-0.4V drop; community standard for eurorack power entry. Vf is 0.24V at 245mA and 0.36V at 612mA, digitised off Fig.2 of the banked DS23001 Rev.8 and calibrated against the two guaranteed points (the method returns 0.454V at 1.0A and 0.746V at 3.0A against specified maxima of 0.450 and 0.750, so +/-0.01V - and THE CURVE SITS ON THE MAX SPEC, so read it typical-to-max). *** THE 1.0A RATING DERATES FROM A LEAD TEMPERATURE OF 90C, NOT AMBIENT, *** falling linearly to 0A at 125C [Fig.1]. With RthJL 15C/W, RthJA 50C/W and ~0.45W at 1.0A, a 65C ambient puts the lead near 81C - inside the knee with roughly 9C of headroom. BUT THAT RthJA IS SPECIFIED FOR THE DATASHEET'S OWN MOUNTING - vertical PCB, 9.5mm leads, 38x38mm copper pads - and a worse mount invalidates the margin. SS34 (Vishay 88751, 3A SMA) and 1N5822 (3A DO-27) are banked as alternatives if E6 measures hot. *** QTY 4: D1 (+12V analog), D3 (-12V analog), and D2/D4, the two legs of U-ISO's input (ADR 0027) - D4 is cathode-to-bus like D3. THE MODULE'S ANALOG RAILS AND THE INSTRUMENT'S SUPPLY MUST NOT SHARE A DIODE. *** The reason is the tracked figure diode-split-rationale, owned by power-entry.md and deliberately not restated here - state it wrongly and the next reviewer who checks the arithmetic deletes the part. The reasons that hold independently of it: fault isolation between the exported rail and the analog rail, and HF isolation (r_d 69 mohm)

description: Adjustable LDO set to 5.21V for the DAC AVDD
notes: Off protected +12V. ~13mA load including the divider, ~90mW. Decouples DAC full scale from the rack's +/-5% +5V rail. TOLERANCE IS A BENCH TASK, NOT A SPEC TASK: worst case spans 0.66V against a ~0.55V window and no nominal value fits on paper, but this is one unit with a TO-92 part, two through-hole resistors and a voltmeter. E7 measures where the DAC's top codes start compressing against AVDD and selects R2 from that - *** BUT NOT BELOW 5.00V, *** because the DAC8568's C grade is specified only for AVDD 5.0-5.5V. *** THE MANUFACTURER FIELD SAYS 'multiple' AND THAT IS DANGEROUS HERE. *** TI's SLCS144E gives minimum output current to maintain regulation as 1.5 typ / 2.5 MAX mA with Io 2.5-100mA - NOT the full LM317's 10mA - while ST's LM317L gives 3.5 typ / 5 MAX mA [ds ST-LM317L-DS2168-REV7.pdf p.7], so 5mA is the worst case to size any bleeder against. The classic Z suffix is an ST/ON TO-92 marking rather than a TI orderable; TI's document covers the LP package. A BLEEDER SIZED FOR TI'S 2.5mA UNDER-LOADS ST'S PART. Either name the manufacturer or size for the worst case across candidates. The ~13mA load clears every reading, so nothing is broken today - the hazard is a future reader trimming the divider current. Reference 1.20/1.25/1.30V confirms the +/-4% claim; line regulation 0.01%/V typ, 0.02%/V max at 25degC on TI's (0.04%/V max on ST's [p.7]); output noise 30uV PER VOLT of output over 10Hz-10kHz, so ~150uV RMS at 5.21V; ripple rejection 65dB typ, rising to 66 min / 80 typ WITH a 10uF cap on ADJUSTMENT - which C-REG-ADJ already fits. PROPOSED: ST LM317LZ, LCSC C5267874. MAP ITS PINS BY NAME: ST numbers the TO-92 1 = ADJ, 2 = IN, 3 = OUT and draws them in the physical order 1-3-2 [ds ST-LM317L-DS2168-REV7.pdf p.4]

description: Series bead per supply branch
notes: One per branch: +12V analog (FB1), -12V analog (FB3), and the two legs of U-ISO's input, FB2 (+12V) and FB4 (-12V) - there is no +5V branch: the module makes its own 5V. Chosen on ONE criterion - it is the only >=1A 600R 1206 part found whose datasheet publishes an IMPEDANCE-UNDER-DC-BIAS curve (traces at 0 / 250 / 500 / 1000 / 1500 mA). Off the drawing: Z@100MHz 600 nominal / 450 min / 750 max, DCR 0.080 ohm max, rated 1500 mA, 3.20 x 1.60 x 1.10 mm, -40 to +125degC including self-heating. *** A BEAD'S CURRENT RATING IS THERMAL, NOT MAGNETIC, so it says nothing about saturation *** - read the bias curve instead. At 100 MHz this part gives ~614 ohm at 0 A, ~431 at 250 mA, ~157 at 500 mA, ~72 at 1000 mA and ~51 at its RATED 1500 mA. Doubling the rating does not help: a 3000 mA twin in the same package reads ~145 ohm at 500 mA, slightly WORSE, for 0.02 ohm more DCR. PER BRANCH: FB3 (-12V, 10-20mA) and FB1 (+12V analog, ~45mA) all sit on the flat part and get 580-614 ohm, essentially the nameplate. *** FB2 AND FB4 CARRY U-ISO's INPUT CURRENT *** - since ADR 0027 about 60% of umbilical-current rather than all of it (power-entry.md), which sits between the flat part and the 250 mA trace: read the bias curve at the real current, not the nameplate. No 1206 600R bead of any rating fixes it; bias shifts the impedance peak UP IN FREQUENCY, so the bead does not die, its useful band slides off 100 MHz. EITHER restate FB2's requirement at its real operating current OR make FB2 a physically larger part. IR drop at 0.080 ohm max is under 20 mV on every branch. SECOND SOURCE: Murata BLM31PG601SN1L is an electrical twin and far better stocked, but its PDF carries no DC-bias curve either - that data lives only in SimSurfing - so it can be an alternate flagged 'bias assumed, not documented', never the characterised part. STOCK: the Laird part is out at LCSC (C2441375, 0). The named Murata twin BLM31PG601SN1L (LCSC C16902) is rated 1500 mA to 85 C and 1000 mA at 125 C [ds MURATA-BLM31-SN1-REFERENCE-SPEC-JENF243A-0006.pdf p.1] - fine at the module's currents - and publishes no DC-bias curve

description: Entry bulk capacitance downstream of each bead
notes: C1 100uF on +12V analog, C3 47uF on -12V. (C2, which was the third, is U-ISO's input bulk now: C-ISO-BULK.) NOT 47uF on both rails. The +12V branch carries the LM317's divider, the DAC and the comparator, about 22mA against -12V's 10mA - so at 47uF each it collapses 2.2x faster and every rack power-down leaves the op-amps with V+ near 0 and V- at -6 to -8V for ~30ms, pulling all six jacks toward the surviving negative rail. 100uF on +12V balances the decay. 10-100uF per rail per ADR 0004; NOT the strip capacitance, which belongs at the load and is C-STRIP-BULK

description: Resettable PTC fuse on each module analog rail, at the header ahead of D1 and D3
notes: PTC-POS12 and PTC-POS12's twin PTC-NEG12: J-PWR-EURO, then the PTC, then the reverse diode (owner, 2026-09-30: 'You're good to add the PTCs'). What they protect is the RACK from a short inside the module; the instrument's supply has its own, PTC-ISO. SIZED ON power-entry.md ('Fuses on the rails'), not here. From the banked datasheet [ds BOURNS-MF-MSMF.pdf p.1, p.9]: Ihold 0.20A / Itrip 0.40A at 23C, 60V, 40A max; Rmin 0.40, R1max 6.0 ohm; hold derates to 0.15A at 50C and 0.13A at 60C. 60V BECAUSE A SHORT BETWEEN THE TWO ANALOG RAILS PUTS 24V ACROSS THE PAIR, and whichever trips first sees it all. LCSC C719178, 5790 in stock [web LCSC 2026-09-30]

description: Resettable PTC fuse in the +12V leg of U-ISO's input, ahead of D2
notes: THE CONVERTER BRANCH'S FUSE, AND RECOM'S INPUT FUSE: F1 in its filter [ds RECOM-RPA20-AW.pdf PD-7], 'Recommended fuse: 3A slow blow type', 'if input over-current protection is also required' [PD-5 Note 5] - a resettable 0.75A-hold part here, because the converter's typical input is ~0.22A and the load switch limits its output. The load switch sits on U-ISO's OUTPUT and cannot see a fault in U-ISO or its input network, so this is what protects the rack from one. ONE LEG IS ENOUGH: the branch is a series loop, +12V through U-ISO to -12V, and C-ISO-Y (the only element from it to ground) hangs on the +12V side. From the banked datasheet [ds BOURNS-MF-MSMF.pdf p.1, p.9]: Ihold 0.75A / Itrip 1.5A at 23C, 33V, 20A max; Rmin 0.11, R1max 0.40 ohm; hold derates to 0.56A at 50C, 0.49A at 60C. 33V BECAUSE A SHORTED U-ISO INPUT PUTS THE WHOLE 24V ACROSS IT. The currents it must hold are on power-entry.md ('Fuses on the rails'). LCSC C3760814, 2770 in stock [web LCSC 2026-09-30]

description: The instrument's isolated supply: 24V (+12 to -12) in, isolated 12V out to the load switch
package: DIP-6 module (pins 1/2/4/5/6 fitted), 25.4 x 25.4 x 10.2mm, pins 5.6mm (woody:Converter_DCDC_RECOM_RPA20-RP20-xxxxSAW_THT)
notes: ADR 0027 (owner, 2026-09-30: 'I thought the point was to do a RECOM that was in stock'). INPUT ACROSS THE RACK'S +12V AND -12V, so the instrument's supply current loops rail to rail and never enters the rack's ground; OUTPUT 12V on ISO_POS12 to U-LOADSW, return on PWR_GND, which meets the module's grounds only through NT-UMB-MOD and NT-DIG-MOD. *** ORDER THE PLAIN RPA20-2412SAW - NO /P, /N OR -HC SUFFIX. *** It has NO CTRL PIN (always on) and a TRIM PIN, left open for 12V nominal [ds RECOM-RPA20-AW.pdf PD-1 Note 2]. From the banked datasheet [ds RECOM-RPA20-AW.pdf, REV 10/2026]: 9-36V in, 24V nominal, 50V surge 100ms; UVLO on 8/8.5/9V, off 7/7.5/8V; quiescent 20/55mA typ/max; switching 550kHz; ripple 50mVp-p (PD-2); 12V at 1670mA, 88% typ at full load, ~81% at the ~21% load of typical play (PD-3 curve, 24V in), max capacitive load 1000uF (PD-1); output accuracy +/-2.0% max, line +/-0.2% max, load +/-0.1%, tempco 0.02%/K; OCP 110-160% of Iout, hiccup - THE MINIMUM, 1.84A, IS ABOVE THE LT1641's 1.10A WORST-CASE TRIP, so the load switch decides every start and every fault; OTP 110C; 1.6kVDC; ISOLATION CAPACITANCE 1100pF TYP (PD-5); 12.5K/W on a PCB in still air (PD-6). RECOM's filter [PD-7]: F1, a 1uH choke and 47uF/50V - L-ISO-IN, C2 and C-ISO-IN are that filter with more L and C; its fuse, 3A slow blow 'if input over-current protection is also required' [PD-5 Note 5], is PTC-ISO. No common-mode choke. HEIGHT 10.2mm plus 5.6mm pins: on module-main's REAR face (config/module.yaml iso.*). *** EOL: 'NOT RECOMMENDED FOR NEW DESIGNS - LAST TIME BUY 6TH JULY 2026' on every page. BUY SPARES NOW. *** DigiKey RPA20-2412SAW-ND, Obsolete, 20 in stock, $53.19 at 1 / $51.22 at 5 / $50.38 at 10 [web digikey.com/en/products/detail/recom-power/RPA20-2412SAW/6206332, 2026-09-30]. FUTURE SUPPLY: RECOM's named successor, the plain RP20-2412SAW, drops into the SAME HOLES with the same function in each [ds RECOM-RP20-AW.pdf PD-6] - only its numbering differs (-Vout 6, +Vout 4, no Trim pin), so the footprint's pads 4 and 6 swap and nothing else. It also differs electrically: OLP 150% typ with no minimum, 1500pF max isolation, 9.9mm tall (ADR 0027). DigiKey RP20-2412SAW-ND, Active, $91.76, 0 in stock, 11 weeks [web 2026-09-30]

UCM1H101MCL1GS: tan-delta 0.10, impedance 0.34 ohm at 100kHz, ripple 350mA [ds NICHICON-UCM-SERIES-UCM1E101MCL1GS.pdf p.3]. AN ELECTROLYTIC, NEVER A CERAMIC: its ESR is L-ISO-IN's damping

notes: At U-ISO's +Vin/-Vin pins: the ceramic half of the input filter, which keeps the converter's switching current in a short loop beside its pins - RECOM's filter names no ceramic [ds RECOM-RPA20-AW.pdf PD-7]. 50V because it sits across both rails. description: U-ISO's output capacitor, ISO_POS12 to PWR_GND
notes: U-ISO's output capacitor, well inside the RPA20-2412SAW's 1000uF maximum capacitive load [ds RECOM-RPA20-AW.pdf PD-1] - the instrument's own capacitance is behind the load switch and charged at the LT1641's limit. It is also the reservoir the load switch draws on in the first moments of a hot-plug (power-entry.md). UCM1E101MCL1GS, LCSC C729678 (the C-BUCK-IN part)

description: Across the isolation barrier at U-ISO: ISO_VIN_POS to PWR_GND
notes: The common-mode return beside the converter: the switching edge drives current through U-ISO's isolation capacitance (1100pF typ [ds RECOM-RPA20-AW.pdf PD-5]), and this gives it a path home at the converter instead of round DIG_GND, the star and the ribbon. RECOM's own filter has no Y-capacitor [PD-7]. No safety isolation is claimed - PWR_GND is tied to the module's ground - so a 50V C0G is enough; ON THE +12V SIDE so that PTC-ISO covers it if it fails short. CC0805JRNPO9BN102, LCSC C62774

description: PWR_GND to DIG_GND at the etherCON, pins 6 and 8
